entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Sam Zeller was awarded the W.K.H. Panofsky Prize. The recognition is for co-leadership of MicroBooNE at Fermilab, which advanced next-generation liquid-argon time projection chamber technology for neutrino detection.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab, CERN and SURF crews have started building the first of two cryostats, the insulated containers that will hold liquid argon for DUNE. Fermilab also reports that construction has begun on the detector in South Dakota, and Colorado State University has marked a construction milestone for the project.

entry.title: SBND cross sections
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SBND has measured the total and single-differential inclusive electron-neutrino charged-current cross sections on argon. The authors describe it as the highest-statistics inclusive measurement of this kind on argon to date and the first using the Booster Neutrino Beam. They stress that the channel matters for electron-neutrino appearance searches, both long- and short-baseline.

entry.title: KM3NeT/ARCA diffuse flux
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT has published a search for an all-sky and a Galactic Ridge diffuse neutrino emission using its first ARCA configurations. These had 6, 8, 19 and 21 detection units and a total livetime of 640 days. For the all-sky analysis, the single power-law fit gives a spectral index of 3.00 with uncertainties of +0.30 and -0.35 at 68% credible level.

entry.title: JUNO water purity
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. JUNO needs ultrapure water with a radium concentration below 50 μBq/m3 because the water is in direct contact with the liquid scintillator during filling. A new preprint describes a measurement system sensitive down to 3.9 μBq/m3 and an optimised 100 t/h production process. The process combines selective ion-exchange resin with membrane-based separation.

entry.title: Movable reactor at JUNO
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A preprint proposes placing a movable reactor antineutrino source within about 3 km of the JUNO detector. The aim is a precision on θ13 beyond that of Daya Bay, which the authors say no planned experiment is expected to surpass. They consider a microreactor of order 20 MW thermal and use JUNO's large fiducial mass to collect enough events.

entry.title: Geoneutrino decay limit
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new analysis uses geoneutrinos to test neutrino decay for the first time. The authors compute the signal for visible decay at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+ and JUNO and compare it with published data. They find no evidence of decay that holds across Earth models, and they combine the four experiments to limit the decay of ν1 to ν3.

entry.title: MINERvA open dataset
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A preprint presents a probabilistic surrogate of the MINERvA detector response, trained on an open simulation dataset. It maps generator-level final-state particles and interaction geometry to reconstructed observables. The aim is to let people outside the original collaboration compare interaction models with open neutrino data.

entry.title: CYGNO electron directionality
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The CYGNO collaboration studies how well the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils can be reconstructed in its optical time-projection chamber, using the 50 L LIME prototype. Directionality could help separate solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds. The algorithm estimates the direction from the early part of the ionisation trail, before multiple scattering erases the directional information.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem for seeing a Majorana phase in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem for seeing a Majorana phase in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations. Any completely positive trace-preserving evolution that is covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to the phase. A rate anisotropy can provide an environmental phase reference. This tells a phenomenologist when decoherence could, and when it cannot, make the Majorana phase observable.

entry.title: The authors study whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande can constrain the primary cosmic-ra
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande can constrain the primary cosmic-ray spectrum through the atmospheric neutrino flux. They find that future detectors can distinguish cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even with uncertainties in neutrino cross sections and hadronic interactions. The result bears on the atmospheric flux uncertainties that enter oscillation analyses.

entry.title: Motivated by updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 extending down to about 0.2 TeV, the paper infers the condition
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Motivated by updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 extending down to about 0.2 TeV, the paper infers the conditions for neutrino production near the supermassive black hole. It computes hadronuclear and photomeson neutrino production with the accompanying cascade gamma rays and explores the parameter space with Latin hypercube sampling. It offers a model-independent route from multimessenger data to the properties of the emission region.

entry.title: The paper considers a gauged Lμ−Lτ extension with an ultralight vector boson
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper considers a gauged Lμ−Lτ extension with an ultralight vector boson. Through kinetic mixing with the photon, it generates an extra matter potential in the Sun that modifies MSW flavour conversion. It uses solar neutrino measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD. It shows how solar neutrinos can probe new light mediators.

entry.title: The authors derive semianalytic approximations for the outcome of slow and fast flavour conversions in quasiho
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors derive semianalytic approximations for the outcome of slow and fast flavour conversions in quasihomogeneous neutrino ensembles. They report excellent agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of the mass ordering. Such approximations are intended as subgrid schemes for supernova simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics.

entry.title: The paper asks whether nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals (paleodetectors) could record neutrinos from
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper asks whether nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals (paleodetectors) could record neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae. It includes different neutron-star masses and failed supernovae that form black holes, and it considers the role of the nuclear equation of state. Sensitivity is larger for models with larger neutrino emission, which links a geological detection method to the spread of collapse outcomes.
